extracted.intended_audience: readers/practitioners of classical geometry (geometers constructing arcs, chords, and tables)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and propositions for constructing/dividing arcs, computing chord lengths, and using tabulated multipliers to convert between arcs, chords, diameters, and circumferences in classical Euclidean-style geometry. Includes methods for making regular inscribed figures and remarks on quadrature of the circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal central angles imply equal peripheral arcs and chords
rubrics_metrics.description: If central angles (or points) subtend equal angles at the center, then the corresponding peripheral arcs (periferie) and chords are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual instances: 'onde la periferia.a y aia periferia.y b.e igualc.' and related passages establishing that equal central angles produce equal arcs and equal chords; used repeatedly to deduce equal segments and to construct equal subdivisions of the circumference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide an angle or arc into two equal parts by bisecting the corresponding chord/line
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide an angle (or an arc) into two equal parts, divide the corresponding line (or diameter/chord) into two equal parts and construct the bisector through the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording examples: 'Diuifo in.2.parti igaaii' / 'Diuidcro laiigolo.f c.a.m.2. parti iguali Dalalinea.' Used as the basic step for constructing halves and subsequent recursive subdivisions (quarters, eighths) of arcs/angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of arcs corresponds to proportion of their chords
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of one arc to another matches the proportion of the corresponding chords: e.g., 'la p2opo2tione del arco g.b. al arco b.a ... come la p:opo2rione de la corda.gb.ala corda.ba.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is invoked to transfer proportional relations between arcs to chords and vice versa, enabling computation of unknown chords from known arcs using proportional arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tabulated multipliers (numerical tables) to convert between arcs and chords
rubrics_metrics.description: Find unknown arcs or chords by multiplying the given arc/cord by specified table multipliers (numerical constants like 42, 26, 109, 217, 440, 478, etc.) and dividing by the diameter or other base unit indicated in the tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many procedural passages explain: take the given arc/cord, 'moltiplica per 42' (or other table numbers), then divide by the diameter or by specified divisors to obtain the corresponding chord/arc. The text frequently refers to 'tauole' (tables) and numerical multipliers to place a given arc within the tabulated system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct regular inscribed figures by successive equal subdivisions of the circumference
rubrics_metrics.description: To form a figure with n equal sides inscribed in a circle, divide the circumference (or an arc) into n equal parts (through repeated bisection or appropriate proportional division) and join successive division points to form the polygon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages show constructing quarters, eighths, etc.: divide arc/angle into 2, then again to get 4, 8, etc., and use resulting points to produce sides of regular polygons: 'fare la quarta parte... la quale non fia verrei tuo cofi... la quarta parte del quadrato oda co2da... trarremo od quadrato oda linea'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bisect chord with perpendicular from center to obtain equal subtended arcs/angles
rubrics_metrics.description: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects that chord and the corresponding arc/angle; conversely, bisecting the chord by a diameter/perpendicular determines equal arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as constructional tool: 'fa dafe.acc. e Ha pcrpendicularo. laqualc paflèra per locentro.' This underlies many steps where lines from the center to chord midpoints are drawn to produce equal subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic manipulation of squares and roots to combine segment data
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine lengths by forming sums/differences of squares of lines and extracting roots (radici) to obtain required linear measures (e.g., to compute certain chords or residual segments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text instructs adding 'li quadrati de le linee' and taking roots: 'ogiongnendo li quadrati... la cui radici e poco meno ... piglieremo li quadrati ode linee... barai d quadrato', showing algebraic-geometric computation of lengths via square/square-root arithmetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate arc lengths and chord values by successive refinement using differences made arbitrarily small
rubrics_metrics.description: By subdividing arcs and using tables with finer resolutions, differences between arcs can be made arbitrarily small and thus any desired arc or chord can be approximated to required precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text remarks on dividing arcs until 'la differencia c è cofa infenfibik a l'arco' and using repeated divisions and tabulated values to reach specific arc notations — a practical scheme for approximation and interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate semicircle/quarter-circle measures to diameter and use them to derive other arc/chord measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use known relations of semicircles and quarter-circles (their diameters, areas, and chord properties) as bases for finding other arcs and chords; the quarter/semicircle often used as normalization unit in tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Detto ccrcbio... il diametro... vero la quarta parte del Diametro in tutto larco multiplica...' and constructions that take semicircle/quarter as reference for tabular multipliers and proportional calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of cords and arcs should be organized by convenient units (feet, inches, pertiche, ponti, once, etc.) and used consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing or consulting tables, adopt consistent local measurement units (the text uses pertiche, ponti, piedi, once, oncie, etc.) and perform the indicated multiplications/divisions in those units per the table's conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise repeatedly gives worked numerical combinations with local units (e.g., '8 pertiche e vno pie' ; 'per.42... pertiche.6 e pie...') and instructs how to handle unit conversions during multiplications/divisions when reading or building the 'tauole'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional reasoning transfers between sectors, triangles, and rectilinear segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportions among sectors, triangular slices, and straight-line segments (catheti, bases) are equivalent in many configurations: proportion of a sector equals proportion of corresponding triangle sectors or chord segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages equate proportions of sectors to those of triangles and lines (e.g., 'la p20po2tione oel fcitto2e.o i e4lTetto2C.D e f.e Inagiojc oc la p:opo:rio!ie oel fcito2e.o ei.3l fetto2C*o è f.ccdmmo la p20p02tione oe langolo...'), and use these equivalences to compute unknown parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a reference circle and known chords to locate unknown chord/arc by algebraic combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a circle with known diameter and some known chord(s), one may locate other chords/arcs by algebraic operations (multiplying, adding/subtracting tabulated results, dividing by diameter, taking square roots) using the reference circle as baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions repeatedly show starting from a circle with known diameter/baseline chords and then manipulating tabular multipliers and arithmetic operations to derive the chord of a desired arc: 'prendere larco... moltiplicare per... dividere per il diametro... troveremo'.

rubrics_metrics.name: On the quadrature of the circle: acknowledgement of difficulty and reliance on approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes the difficulty (and perhaps impossibility) of exact quadrature of the circle by classical means, and therefore recommends approximation procedures and tabular methods to approach quadrature-related measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases: 'la difficulta della quadratura del cerchio ... non fia trovata se non quanto per arebimede' and 'la quadratura... si compinde di feconde ... e dabile', indicating acceptance of approximation and tabular/arithmetical techniques rather than a claim of an exact Euclidean quadrature.
